stops.name: Arrive at CPH
stops.desc: Activate the Copenhagen Card in the app, then take the M2 metro from Terminal 3 to Kongens Nytorv, about 15 minutes.
stops.alert: The card is digital only. Activate it in the app before you board.

stops.name: Drop bags at the hotel
stops.note: Short walk from Kongens Nytorv metro

stops.name: Broens Gadekøkken - lunch
stops.desc: Year-round street food square at the foot of the Inner Harbour Bridge. Around a dozen stalls; the Gasoline Grill burger is the usual pick.

stops.name: Nyhavn
stops.desc: The postcard harbour of painted 17th-century townhouses and old wooden ships. Walk the quayside before the tour boats fill up.

stops.name: Canal tour from Nyhavn
stops.desc: About an hour on the water: Christiansborg, the Opera House, Christianshavn and the Little Mermaid from the harbour side. Sit on the open deck if the weather allows.

stops.name: Amalienborg and the Marble Church
stops.desc: The royal residence's four identical palaces around an octagonal square, with the dome of Frederik's Church lined up behind. Free to walk through.

stops.name: Back to hotel
stops.desc: Rest before the evening.

stops.name: Tivoli Gardens
stops.desc: The 1843 pleasure garden in the middle of the city. Go for the evening, when thousands of lights come on. Entry is covered by the card; rides are paid separately. Eat inside the gardens.
stops.note: M3 to Copenhagen Central Station, entrance opposite
stops.alert: Tivoli is seasonal and closes for part of the year. Check the dates before you travel.

days.title: Rosenborg · Round Tower · Christiansborg · Christiania · Reffen

stops.name: GRØD at Torvehallerne - breakfast
stops.desc: The original Copenhagen porridge bar inside the Torvehallerne glass market halls. Oat porridge with caramelised apple is the pick; browse the stalls after.

stops.name: Rosenborg Castle and the King's Garden
stops.desc: Renaissance castle built as Christian IV's summer house, with the Crown Jewels in the vaulted treasury. Allow 1 to 1.5 hours, then walk out through the King's Garden.
stops.alert: Busy on summer weekends. Arrive at opening.

stops.name: Round Tower
stops.desc: A 17th-century observatory with a spiral ramp instead of stairs and a wide view over the old town rooftops. 30 to 45 minutes.
stops.note: 10 min walk south through the Latin Quarter

stops.name: Smørrebrød lunch
stops.desc: Open-faced rye sandwiches are the classic Danish lunch. Plenty of options around Strøget and the Latin Quarter.

stops.name: Christiansborg Palace
stops.desc: Seat of the Danish parliament. The Royal Reception Rooms and the tapestries are the highlight. The tower has one of the best free views in the city.

stops.name: Christianshavn and Christiania
stops.desc: Canal-side streets and houseboats, then Freetown Christiania, the self-governing commune on the old barracks site. Wander the lanes and the lakeside paths.
stops.alert: No photos on Pusher Street, and keep your phone away there.

stops.name: Reffen - dinner
stops.desc: Northern Europe's largest street food market, on the old shipyard at Refshaleøen. Dozens of stalls, bars and harbour-side seating. Stay for sunset over the water.
stops.alert: Seasonal, roughly mid-March to the end of September.

stops.name: Back to hotel
stops.note: Harbour bus or bus 2A back to the centre

days.title: Østerbro · Little Mermaid · Design · Kødbyen · Carlsberg · Airport

stops.name: Juno the Bakery - breakfast
stops.desc: Small Østerbro bakery known for its cardamom buns. Expect a queue on weekends, and they can sell out.

stops.name: Kastellet and the Little Mermaid
stops.desc: Walk the ramparts of the star-shaped 17th-century fortress, then down to the harbour for Edvard Eriksen's statue. Smaller than people expect.

stops.name: Design Museum Denmark
stops.desc: Danish furniture and industrial design in a former hospital. The chair hall is the highlight. Allow about an hour.

stops.name: Kødbyen - lunch
stops.desc: The Meatpacking District, now bars and restaurants in the old white-tiled halls. WarPigs does Texas-style brisket by weight.
stops.note: M3 to Copenhagen Central Station, 10 min walk

stops.name: Home of Carlsberg
stops.desc: The historic brewery site, with the Elephant Gate, the stables and a tasting at the end. Allow about 1.5 hours.

stops.name: Collect bags
stops.note: Back to the hotel near Kongens Nytorv

stops.name: Head to CPH - flight departs 19:30
stops.desc: Aim to be at the airport two hours before departure.
stops.note: M2 from Kongens Nytorv to the airport, about 15 minutes
stops.alert: The 72h card started Friday 10:00, so it still covers this trip.

tips.title: Copenhagen Card
tips.text: The DISCOVER card covers 80+ attractions and all public transport in the Capital Region, including the airport metro and harbour buses. It is digital and lives in the app. A 72h card started on arrival covers the whole weekend.

tips.title: Bikes have right of way
tips.text: Cycle lanes are busy and fast. Look both ways before stepping off the kerb, and never stand in a bike lane.

tips.title: Card, not cash
tips.text: Almost everywhere is card-only or card-preferred. Prices are in Danish kroner.

tips.title: Weather
tips.text: It can be windy along the harbour even in summer. Bring a light layer for the canal tour and Reffen in the evening.
